story: What it's like to use Haskell
text: It's good to hear stories about how FP is being used in industry and I'd like to read more. For those who have an interest in this, I recommend the Commercial Users of Functional Programming workshop ( [LINK] ). It's where I first heard about Facebook's use of OCaml to create Hack ( [VIDEO] )

I tried looking for something by way of an official announcement or release (preview or otherwise), but as Keith Adams joked, it's impossible it Google it, and the [LINK] URL he referenced is not correct. Someone in the Q&A pointed that out, so he mentioned that there'd be a post about it on the HHVM blog, but there doesn't seem to be anything about it in the last few months (this talk took place in September). Someone asked Keith Adams on Twitter at the end of October, where Adams said there was nothing to announce yet: [LINK] The only other thing I could find about it was another talk by Julien Verlaguet (to whom Adams credits the invention of Hack) from October: [VIDEO]

> Last time I checked, the ability to write Javascript using both languages was of experimental and/or novelty use only (hence the "cupholders"). Facebook uses an OCaml js_of_ocaml-based frontend for a large chunk of their production code editing. Not a great video, but here's the CUFP 2013 talk on the topic: [VIDEO]
